fm.title: Analysis enhancement
fm.description: HDL-optimized feature detection and image enhancement on a pixel stream (3 blocks)

rows.intent: HDL-optimized corner detector on a pixel stream — use for hardware feature/interest-point detection (Harris/FAST-style).
HDL-optimized edge detector on a pixel stream — use for hardware edge extraction (Sobel/Prewitt/Roberts).
HDL-optimized median filter on a pixel stream — use for hardware impulse-noise (salt-and-pepper) removal that preserves edges.

fm.title: Conversions
fm.description: HDL-optimized color, gamma, and format conversions (5 blocks)

rows.intent: HDL-optimized chroma resampler that converts between chroma-subsampling formats (4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0) — use in hardware video pipelines.
HDL-optimized color space conversion (e.g., RGB↔YCbCr) on a pixel stream — use in hardware video pipelines.
HDL-optimized demosaic that reconstructs full RGB from a Bayer sensor pattern — use as the first stage of a hardware camera pipeline.
HDL-optimized gamma correction on a pixel stream — use for hardware tone/gamma adjustment.
HDL-optimized per-pixel lookup table — use for hardware intensity remapping and point operations on a pixel stream.
Informational block linking to Vision HDL Toolbox example models — not used in production designs.

fm.title: Filtering
fm.description: HDL-optimized spatial filters on a pixel stream (3 blocks)

rows.intent: HDL-optimized edge-preserving bilateral filter on a pixel stream — use for hardware noise reduction that keeps edges sharp.
HDL-optimized general 2-D FIR image filter with a user kernel on a pixel stream — use for hardware convolution such as blur, sharpen, or emboss.
HDL-optimized median filter on a pixel stream — use for hardware impulse-noise (salt-and-pepper) removal that preserves edges.

fm.title: Geometric transforms
fm.description: HDL-optimized geometric warps and resizing (2 blocks)

rows.intent: HDL-optimized bird's-eye (inverse-perspective) transform on a pixel stream — use to generate a top-down view in hardware.
HDL-optimized image resizer (scaling) on a pixel stream — use for hardware up/downscaling of video.

fm.title: Morphology
fm.description: HDL-optimized morphological operations on a pixel stream (8 blocks)

rows.intent: HDL-optimized binary morphological closing on a pixel stream — use to fill small holes and gaps in hardware.
HDL-optimized binary morphological dilation on a pixel stream — use to grow foreground regions in hardware.
HDL-optimized binary morphological erosion on a pixel stream — use to shrink foreground regions and remove speckle in hardware.
HDL-optimized grayscale morphological closing on a pixel stream — use to remove small dark features while preserving intensity.
HDL-optimized grayscale morphological dilation on a pixel stream — use to expand bright regions in hardware.
HDL-optimized grayscale morphological erosion on a pixel stream — use to shrink bright regions in hardware.
HDL-optimized grayscale morphological opening on a pixel stream — use to remove small bright features while preserving intensity.
HDL-optimized binary morphological opening on a pixel stream — use to remove small bright specks in hardware.

fm.title: Statistics
fm.description: HDL-optimized image statistics on a pixel stream (2 blocks)

rows.intent: HDL-optimized image histogram on a pixel stream — use for hardware intensity-distribution analysis and equalization.
HDL-optimized running image statistics (mean/variance) on a pixel stream — use for hardware exposure control and frame analysis.

fm.title: Utilities
fm.description: Pixel-stream control, buffering, and timing helpers (8 blocks)

rows.intent: Track the horizontal and vertical pixel coordinates within a video frame — use to locate the current pixel in a hardware stream.
Buffer lines of a pixel stream to form pixel neighborhoods — use as the building block for hardware kernel/window operations.
Measure the timing of a pixel-control stream (active/blanking region and frame size) — use to validate video timing in hardware.
Select individual signals (hStart, vStart, valid, hEnd, vEnd) from the pixel-control bus — use to access streaming control flags.
Align two pixel streams so their control signals coincide — use to synchronize streams before combining them in hardware.
Extract one or more rectangular regions of interest from a pixel stream — use to process only part of a frame in hardware.

Creates a pixelcontrol bus. The block has 5 input ports: hStart - First pixel in a horizontal line of a frame hEnd - Last pixel in a horizontal line of a frame vStart - First pixel in the first (top) line of a frame vEnd - Last pixel in the last (bottom) line of a frame valid - Valid pixel indicator
Buffer bursts of pixels into a contiguous stream
